html:
The Komnenian restoration is the recovery of the Byzantine Empire under emperors of the Komnenos family, from 1081 to 1185. Three able emperors rebuilt the army, the money and the standing of an empire that had nearly collapsed after the defeat at Manzikert in 1071.

  • Alexios I (1081 to 1118) beat the Normans and Pechenegs, reformed the coinage and used the First Crusade to win back western Anatolia.
  • John II (1118 to 1143) fought on every frontier and regained land in Anatolia and Syria.
  • Manuel I (1143 to 1180) made Byzantium again a great Mediterranean power, but lost to the Seljuks at Myriokephalon in 1176.

The recovery rested on family rule. Power and land went to relatives by blood and marriage, and soldiers were paid with pronoia grants. Trade privileges for Italian cities, first Venice, bought alliances but cost income. After Manuel's death the violent reign of Andronikos I ended the dynasty in 1185, and twenty years later came the sack of Constantinople.
